result.title: Cross-Market Meta-Learning for Electricity Price Forecasting
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI Foundations for Power Grids
result.summary: Day-ahead (DA) electricity price forecasting is usually posed per market, with a separate model fitted to each grid's own history. This caps accuracy: statistical and tree-based baselines saturate, while higher-capacity sequence models need more training data than a single market's few years of hourly prices can supply. Such methods also treat each node as an independent series, discarding the spatial dependencies induced by network topology and congestion. Because price formation across independent system operators (ISOs) is driven by shared physics and largely common market design, we instead treat cross-market history as a pretraining corpus. We present MetaGrid, a topology-aware transformer, meta-trained across markets so that a single zone-count-independent parameter set adapts to an unseen grid. On a leak-free benchmark of five U.S. ISOs, where every model receives the same prices, DA load forecasts and calendar features, MetaGrid attains the lowest average MAE, improving on the best baseline by 3.1\% and on the same architecture trained from scratch by 7.7\%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MetaGrid，一个拓扑感知 transformer，把多个电力市场历史当作预训练语料做跨市场元训练，使单一、与区域数无关的参数集能适应未见电网，并在五个美国 ISO 的无泄漏基准上取得最低平均 MAE。
AI.relevance_reason: 跨域元训练得到可迁移到未见拓扑、不依赖节点数的单一参数集，与 LVR 关注的长度／规模泛化及预测工作区如何适应新结构可能存在可核查的类比线索，但属较远领域，需人工判断迁移价值。
